Treaties are to be interpreted in good faith, according to the ordinary meaning of their terms in context and in light of the treaty's object and purpose (Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties 1969, Art. 31(1)). Context includes the text, preamble, annexes, related agreements, subsequent practice and relevant rules of international law, and supplementary means such as the preparatory work (travaux préparatoires) may be used only to confirm that meaning or when it remains ambiguous or leads to an absurd result (Art. 32). Special meanings apply only if the parties so intended, and where texts in several authentic languages differ, the meaning that best reconciles them is adopted (Arts. 31(4), 33).

CONFIDENCE: 96
